$comment: Angular internal portal, deployed to its own Firebase Hosting site.
The portal and the public site live in the same repo but deploy
independently: separate sites means separate release history and separate
rollback, and neither has to be rebuilt when the other changes. The cost is
that the two are different origins, so they share no cookies or local
storage and calls between them are cross-origin.
Because the app owns its site root, nothing in the source needs a base path:
Auth0 redirects off window.location.origin and the PWA manifest's scope of
'/' are both already correct.
appRoot is set, so the deploy artifact is staged from appRoot/outputPath and
Firebase's 'public' dir = outputPath. outputPath follows angular.json, where
outputPath.base is 'dist/internal' and @angular/build:application nests the
browser bundle under 'browser/'.
configTemplate is the PWA template rather than the plain one. The plain
template marks every .js immutable for a year, which would pin the service
worker and stop any later release from reaching a browser that has already
registered it. 'ng build' defaults to the production configuration, which
sets serviceWorker in angular.json, so this app always ships one.
Doppler must supply the app's NG_APP_* values; they are inlined into the
browser bundle at build time and the build fails to compile on a missing key.
